Article Title: Pravesh Verma slap row: AAP leaders Saurabh Bharadwaj, Jarnail Singh detained after FIR over cop assault
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Several Aam Aadmi Party leaders including Saurabh Bharadwaj and MLA Jarnail Singh were detained outside the Delhi Police headquarters during a protest on Tuesday, demanding an FIR against Delhi minister Pravesh Varma for slapping a person during a road inspection in West Delhi’s Tilak Nagar.An FIR has also been registered against Bharadwaj, Jarnail Singh and other for allegedly assaulting a head constable during the protest."An FIR has been registered regarding the assault on a Delhi Police head constable. The FIR mentions the names of Saurabh Bharadwaj, Jarnail Singh, and AAP workers. An FIR has also been registered against Sahib Singh. Arvind Kejriwal had visited Tilak Nagar yesterday," Delhi Police said."The Delhi Police head constable was recording a video while in plain clothes. A crowd of AAP supporters surrounded and assaulted him. Subsequently, the Head Constable underwent a medical examination. A case has been registered under sections related to obstructing a public servant in the discharge of official duties and assaulting a public servant," it added.The complaint comes amid a political row over an alleged slapping incident involving Verma during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar on September 27.A purported video of the incident was shared by AAP leaders, showing Verma allegedly slapping Singh during a confrontation over the quality of a newly constructed road.Speaking to ANI before his detention during an AAP protest outside Vikaspuri police station, Bharadwaj alleged that Verma attacked the cameraman after AAP MLA Jarnail Singh demonstrated the poor quality of the road."When Jarnail Singh—in the presence of minister Parvesh Verma and the camera—demonstrated the poor quality of the road by breaking off a piece with his hands to expose the corruption and embezzlement of funds in road construction, Parvesh Verma flew into a rage. He attacked the cameraman, snatched his phone, slapped him, and attempted to destroy the evidence of corruption; when the young man lunged back towards him, he fled in fear and hid behind the police," Bharadwaj had said.Meanwhile, Sahib Singh, who alleged that Verma slapped him during the road inspection, claimed that the minister snatched his phone, twisted his arm and assaulted him after the condition of the road was highlighted. Singh also alleged that the police accepted his complaint but did not register an FIR against Verma.
Article Summary: Several Aam Aadmi Party leaders detained outside the Delhi Police headquarters. Delhi minister Pravesh Varma allegedly slapped a person during a road inspection in West Delhi’s Tilak Nagar. An FIR has also been registered against Bharadwaj, Jarnail Singh and other.

Article Title: Assam Rifles jawan killed, four injured in suspected militant attack along Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh
Article Text:
Suspected militant attack along India-Myanmar border (ANI file photo)

NEW DELHI: An Assam Rifles jawan was killed and four others injured after a patrol team came under suspected militant attack along the India-Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district on Tuesday, news agency PTI cited officials.The incident took place around 6.30am near Nampong Nallah under Nampong circle, when personnel of the 21 Assam Rifles were patrolling an area where border fencing work is under way.Preliminary reports suggested that suspected militants opened fire on the patrol team, killing Havildar Jankhokai Kuki, 42, and injuring four others.The injured personnel were being evacuated for medical treatment.Details about their condition were not immediately available.Security forces have intensified operations in the area following the attack, officials said.Preliminary reports indicated the involvement of militants belonging to the NSCN (K-YA), though there was no official confirmation about the identity of the attackers.An official statement from the Assam Rifles is awaited.Changlang SP Kirli Padu said police had received information about the incident and directed the officer-in-charge of Changlang police station to gather details."We have received information about the incident that took place along the India-Myanmar border and have asked the OC of Changlang police station to collect information related to it," Padu said.The India-Myanmar border in Changlang district has remained sensitive because of the movement of insurgent groups operating in the region and across the international boundary.
Article Summary: An Assam Rifles jawan was killed and four others injured after a patrol team came under suspected militant attack. The incident took place along the India- Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district. Security forces have intensified operations in the area following the attack.

Article Title: India needs heritage zones, not heritage islands
Article Text:
Advantages

Higher footfalls in the heritage zone itself, which would especially benefit less-known monuments.

Optimal utilization of space in the heritage zone, bringing in new audiences causing benefits to both the monument’s eyeballs as well as the Haat.

Seamless cultural connection between handicrafts and heritage zones building a multi-sensory journey encompassing architecture, craft and culture.

Ensures neglected parts of a large heritage zone are spruced up and not left to be covered by vegetation or intruded by anti-social elements.

Creates economic opportunities, both to the artisans and to the agency managing the monument. A revenue sharing arrangement could be explored.

Challenges

Process

Curation of such a zone will need to be pioneered by the Union Ministry of Culture, bringing in subject matter experts from the private sector or non-for-profit bodies such as the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH).

Monitoring the heritage zone to ensure the monument stays untouched is a task for the ASI, of or state department, if it is a state managed monument.

Pan-India model

(The author is a heritage enthusiast)

At the end of August this year, the Prime Minister visited Uzbekistan. Had his visit been a trifle longer and encompassed the Registan complex in Samarkand, he may have come across an interesting feature in the madrasas that constitute the complex. Within each madrasa, the cells where students once lived are now shops for handicrafts, bridging the gap between architectural history and living heritage. The marketplace does not just bring alive the otherwise passive monument, it also creates a ‘heritage zone’ compelling visitors to spend more time and adds to the local economy. This phenomenon of creating heritage zones, common in that country, is something India would do well to learn from.A visitor to the Qutab Minar complex in Delhi, also a UNESCO World Heritage site like the Registan Square, sees a set of magnificent monuments. However, the place gives no clue about the larger heritage ecosystem that lies just beyond the walls of the Qutab complex. And importantly, the opportunity to create a showcase of living heritage too has been missed.Sharing a wall with the Qutab complex is Mehrauli Archaeological Park, dotted with tombs, mosques, a magnificent stepwell, stables, cupolas as well as some British era structures.On the other side of the complex lies Mehrauli village, with more tombs, a dargah, the Zafar Mahal, another stepwell and a tiny World War I marker. Nothing in the Qutab complex indicates the existence of this larger heritage universe.Nor is there any mention of the superb Dastkar Haat, a short drive away. In March this year, the Haat saw a major fire that destroyed over forty shops and caused losses of several crore. To anyone who has visited the place, it is apparent that the Haat suffers from a lack of space. On the other side, the Mehrauli Archaeological Park, spread over 200 acres, lacks publicity and footfalls. The back wall of the park is broken and serves as a thoroughfare for people in Mehrauli village. After dark come the unsavoury elements. An uncovered drain flows through a part of the park. The logical solution would be to marry the two spaces.Imagine a scenario where visitors had an option to exit – or enter - the Qutab complex into the Archaeological Park, in one corner of which the Dastkar Haat is relocated. Currently the park has a solitary café. Create more such cafes and even fine dining areas, as well as an amphitheatre enabling cultural performances and open-air exhibitions.The biggest plus is to create urban spaces in and around hitherto neglected heritage zones that ensure:The Dastkar Haat is a creation of a non-profit society which runs for the welfare of artisans, in partnership with Delhi Tourism. The latter reports to the Delhi State Government while the Delhi Development Authority – which controls the park – is under the Central Government’s Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. The monuments are with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), under the jurisdiction of the Central Government’s Ministry of Culture. Imagine the sheer number of bureaucrats involved and the resultant turf war. Adding to the confusion are some madrasas, supposedly under the umbrella of the Waqf Board, which are functioning out of monuments.The suggestion of bringing a Haat into the vicinity of a space that has the Jamali-Kamali mosque, Balban’s tomb and the Rajaon-ki-Baoli would instantly anger heritage hardliners, not to mention ASI officials.This model ‘heritage zone’ already exists in Sunder Nursery and begs to be implemented in sites across India. The nursery was once a mere offshoot of the Humayun’s Tomb complex, drawing in only flora and heritage afficionados.Today, it is a magnificent cultural hub.Imagine the Tughlakabad Fort as a place for musical evenings instead of being overgrown with scrub. Imagine if the National Crafts Museum were not in isolation in a corner of Bharat Mandapam but within the Purana Qila complex. Imagine if the neglected spaces near Ujjain’s Kaliyadeh Palace were leveraged to create a crafts bazaar. Imagine if Chhattisgarh’s tribal art, crafts and cuisine were to be given a space – even on a seasonal basis – at the heritage hub of Sirpur. Imagine!
Article Summary: The Dastkar Haat is located in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The Qutab Minar complex in Delhi is also a UNESCO World Heritage site. Mehrauli Archaeological Park, spread over 200 acres, lacks publicity and footfalls.

Article Title: Delhi HC quashes FSSAI order directing Red Bull to drop 'energy drink' label
Article Text:
The court set said the decision was taken “without affording any opportunity” to the company to present its views.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Tuesday quashed an order issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) directing Austrian beverage maker Red Bull to stop using the “energy drink” descriptor on its cans.The court set aside the June 30, 2026 order, saying that the regulator had taken the decision “without affording any opportunity” to the company to present its views.The order came after Red Bull challenged the FSSAI directive, which required the company to remove the “energy drink” descriptor from its range of caffeinated beverages.Red Bull had approached the Delhi HC on Monday, challenging the FSSAI order issued by an Assistant Director on June 30. The company said it had been selling its products in India since 2002 using the “energy drink” descriptor.During Monday's hearing, Justice Amit Mahajan sought clarity from FSSAI on whether Red Bull had been issued a show-cause notice and given an opportunity to explain its position before the order was passed.The court also questioned the need for immediate action without first hearing the company and asked FSSAI to take instructions on the matter.No interim protection was granted to Red Bull during Monday’s proceedings.Red Bull also challenged a July 17 communication issued by FSSAI to food safety authorities across states and Union Territories, directing them to take action against allegedly non-compliant products.According to the company’s petition, the June 30 direction was issued without prior notice or an opportunity of hearing. Red Bull further claimed that the July communication led to enforcement action, including the seizure of its products at various locations across the country.The company has questioned the basis for the change in FSSAI’s position, citing a March 2024 advisory which, according to its petition, had clarified that the expression “energy drink” could be used for products falling under the relevant food categories applicable to caffeinated beverages.Earlier in June, India directed makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as “energy drinks” to stop using the description, rejecting efforts to stall the move in a market expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, Reuters reported.Red Bull’s India unit had said the “abrupt prohibition” of the label, without any change to the underlying product standard, “introduces substantial regulatory uncertainty and adversely affects” its existing and planned commercial investments.Energy drinks have faced scrutiny from regulators in several countries over concerns about their high caffeine, sugar and taurine content. England is also set to ban the sale of energy drinks to children under 16 from April next year.
Article Summary: Red Bull challenged the FSSAI directive, which required the company to remove the “energy drink” descriptor from its range of caffeinated beverages. The court set said the decision was taken “without affording any opportunity” to theCompany to present its views.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi backs Gen Z protests: 'Stop punishing women for crimes against them'
Article Text:
"Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday backed the ongoing student-led protests over women’s safety, accusing the government of responding to violence against women by restricting their movement instead of making public spaces safer.His remarks came amid renewed protests in Delhi following the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in south Delhi. Hundreds of students, many of them women, have taken to the streets over the past week demanding safer public spaces, stronger policing and greater accountability."Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X."Across our country, women are afraid to walk the streets, afraid of being harassed, afraid of being raped. And the government’s answer: stay at home," he said.Rahul Gandhi argued that asking women to restrict their movement amounted to victim-blaming instead of addressing the conditions that make public spaces unsafe."This is patriarchy at work: a system that blames the victim and shields the criminal. It is time to smash it," he said.The Congress leader said the focus should instead be on making streets safer, challenging attitudes that enable violence against women and ensuring swift punishment for offenders."The solution is not to lock women inside. It is to make our streets safe, to confront the mindset of men who mistreat women, and to punish those who attack them, swiftly and without exception," the Congress leader said.Protests over the Aastha Kunj case have grown across Delhi University. Students from institutions including Lady Shri Ram College, Miranda House, Gargi College and BR Ambedkar University have participated in demonstrations, raising concerns over harassment, poorly lit streets and restrictions imposed on women because of safety fears.The issue has also reached the Supreme Court. On Monday, the court questioned the Delhi government and police over recent crimes against women and girls in the national capital and sought accountability over what it described as failures in ensuring public safety.Rahul Gandhi urged more young people, particularly women from Gen Z, to join peaceful protests."Thousands of students and young people are on the streets demanding safety for women. I urge even more young women, especially GenZ across India to come out in stronger numbers," he said."This government is deaf to your pain and will only listen when it’s under pressure. Peaceful protest is your democratic right, and I stand with you wholeheartedly," he added.Creative placards and slogans such as "Abort Patriarchy", "My favourite season is FALL of patriarchy", "Bas bohot ho gaya" (enough is enough), and "Bade bade shehron mein aisi chhoti soch nahi chalegi" (such a narrow mindset will not work in big cities) stood out as protesters marched through the campus amid heavy police presence.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses government of responding to violence against women by restricting their movement. His remarks come amid renewed protests in Delhi following the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl. Hundreds of students, many of them women, have taken to the streets over the past week.

Article Title: 'Excluding Citizens Intentionally': Congress calls ECINet BJP's 'star campaigner' amid SIR row
Article Text:
Congress leader Surjewala questions ECINet over voter roll revision, alleges centralised control

ECI now officially stands for Excluding Citizens Intentionally: Surjewala

21.1% voters missing from Maharashtra draft roll

EC moves to review ECINet system

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Randeep Singh Surjewala on Tuesday alleged that the Election Commission’s centralised ECINet software was restricting the powers of ground-level election officials and could lead to the exclusion of eligible voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Surjewala cited the Maharashtra chief electoral officer’s concerns over ECINet and alleged that the system was limiting the ability of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to independently resolve discrepancies in voter records.The Maharashtra CEO had written to the Election Commission seeking changes to ECINet, including greater discretion for EROs in dealing with logical discrepancies and provisions to ease requirements for certain voters. The request came amid the ongoing SIR exercise in the state.Citing the Indian Express Report, Surjewala also flagged the 21.1% reduction in the number of electors in Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll following the SIR exercise. The draft roll contained around 7.72 crore electors, compared with about 9.79 crore in the previous roll.The reduction does not mean that all these voters have been permanently deleted.Maharashtra election authorities have said the excluded voters can seek inclusion through the claims process, with the reasons for non-inclusion including voters being absent, shifted, dead or duplicate entries.The EC has meanwhile ordered a review of the ECINet system amid concerns over its functioning during the SIR process. A committee headed by a senior deputy election commissioner, with an independent expert has been tasked with examining whether the system complies with the relevant laws and rules.The poll panel has also eased the procedure for voters who receive notices during the SIR process. Under the revised arrangement, Booth Level Officers can visit voters’ homes, collect supporting documents and upload them on ECINet for the ERO to take a final decision, instead of routinely requiring voters to appear in person.
Article Summary: Congress leader Randeep Singh Surjewala questions ECINet over voter roll revision, alleges centralised control. EC moves to review ECinet system amid concerns over its functioning during the SIR process. The draft roll contained around 7.72 crore electors, compared with about 9.79 crore in the previous roll.

Article Title: Lack of empathy over terror concerns, trade 'bump': Jaishankar explains what weighs on India-US ties
Article Text:
Jaishankar said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement.

India-US ties

: Trade talks remain a key issue

Jaishankar says India-China ties improving

Ukraine, Iran conflicts pose risks to Global South

'World moving towards greater multipolarity'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday flagged a lack of “understanding or appreciation or empathy” in the US towards India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism, saying the issue has affected bilateral ties.Speaking at the Asia Society in New York after the conclusion of the UN General Assembly’s High-Level Week, Jaishankar said terrorism remains a key concern for India, given its experience of cross-border attacks over several decades.“Terrorism emanating from its neighbour is one of India’s primary concerns, and if this is not fully appreciated by New Delhi's partners, it impacts bilateral ties,” Jaishankar said, in an apparent reference to India-US relations amid closer engagement between Washington and Islamabad.“What for us in India is particularly important is the issue of terrorism... There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbor as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many decades. It is something which matters so deeply to us. There isn't enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that. I think that creates a problem too,” he said.Jaishankar also discussed the challenges facing India-US relations, including negotiations on a trade agreement.He said the talks were complex because of the fundamental differences between the two economies, including India’s large base of small producers, farmers and factories.“Much of the world has had a more difficult relationship with the US... In our case, one was the trade negotiation. If you look at the stakes involved, the complexity of it involved, bear in mind, India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, small factories. Apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production and the nature of society are very different. A trade negotiation required a certain amount of patience and detailing to see it through,” he said.Jaishankar said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement, but changes in the US tariff framework had created a new challenge.“We have reached a situation where there is more or less an understanding on the trade agreement. But as my trade minister has said on more than one occasion, the issue is now what has changed on the American side. On the American side, reciprocal tariffs were struck down. So there's now a new basis for tariff imposition, which is 301. And the 301 process is still in the works... that did create bumps last year for the relationship. If that agreement is closed out, that would be one point which would contribute to a better relationship,” he added.He also highlighted the growing influence of public opinion on diplomacy, particularly in democratic countries, saying social media had added a new dimension to international relations.“Today the economics of mobility and the politics of mobility are at odds with each other.... That certainly, in public perception, is an issue... our diplomacy today is not just conducted by states, leaders, ministers, or even by diplomats. In a social media era, there is a very big public opinion factor, which, particularly in democratic societies, makes itself felt. I think that's a reality we have to take into account. .. We would certainly hope for and expect the relationship to move on an upward trajectory. But I have to be real about the issues that we confront. And to the extent we are able to move ahead on some of these issues, I think we'll have a better relationship. Let's apply the lens of...”On India-China relations, Jaishankar said ties were better than they were in 2025 and had improved further compared with 2024, pointing to the easing of the border standoff.“If you asked me, compared to where you were in 2025, is the relationship better today? I would say yes. Compared to 2024, even more so... After what happened in 2020 and the long standoff that we had on the border, the relationship had really been impacted... once the border standoff was resolved, it was natural that this would start to improve,” he said.Jaishankar said India had consistently conveyed to Beijing that a prolonged standoff between the two countries would not benefit either side.“We have long been telling the Chinese, personally at my level, that a standoff between us, a dip in our relationship, doesn't help either of us. Third parties will take advantage of that... It took a little while for the Chinese side to agree with that, for whatever reason. But I don't think that long standoff served our interests. It certainly didn't serve theirs... what we've had is that, as the border comes back more towards normalcy, the relationship comes back more towards normalcy. .. If it happens, it helps both of us,” he said.He said the two countries had arrived at a basic principle that the state of the border determines the broader state of the relationship.“We came down to a very fundamental principle, which is that the state of the border determines the state of the relationship. You can't have tension...on the border and say the relationship should be normal. So what we've had is, as the border comes back more towards normalcy, the relationship comes back more towards normalcy, and if the relationship comes back more towards normalcy, it helps both of us,” Jaishankar said.Jaishankar also highlighted the economic impact of the Ukraine and Iran-Gulf conflicts on developing economies, particularly through energy and food security.“If you look at these two conflicts, the Ukraine and the Iran-Gulf conflict, they've actually had a devastating impact on Global South economies. We are particularly concerned about the energy situation, because the market is very tight. On top of that, if people play politics with it, it adds to the market complications. It will drive up prices at a time when people should be stabilizing prices. A part of it is the security of oil supplies, and another is the politics of oil supplies. They are feeding into each other. They're creating a double crisis or an aggravated crisis,” he said.“When it comes to food, we are looking at a situation today where some of the major grain exporters will not be able to send out their shipments... We are looking at significant fertilizer shortages... On top of it, we are looking at Super El Niño. There is going to be a major food crisis, probably in the coming months...” he added.Jaishankar said the world was moving “quite visibly” towards greater multipolarity and outlined what he described as a broader approach India could pursue in such an environment.He said countries that were seen as stable, consistent and reliable could become important partners as the global order becomes more competitive.“One, you build a reputation for yourself as stable, consistent, reliable, so that others view you in a very dynamic, volatile world as a steadying factor... Partners tend to gravitate towards you. You're the good person in the neighborhood. The second would be that the more you diversify and you find common interests, common ground, I think the more of a balancing structure can be created. What we have to do is to take self-interest and temper it with a certain long-term, I would say, predictability and stability, which is also part of intelligent self-interest, and try to create something along those lines. ..”He said countries, particularly major trading economies, would seek stability rather than prolonged volatility saying, “...not everybody wants the Hobbesian scenario that you painted; it is very volatile. It's actually very risky in real life. People will not expose their trade accounts to that kind of volatility. For the big trading countries, their economies are exposed to that. Everybody will want to find some accounts of stability... I think the world will go for that kind of mix... The world is more competitive. It's tough. A new dynamic will come.""A new culture will come. New negotiations and new bargains will be struck. When the smoke clears at some point in time, you will see the different points joined by lines of different lengths. There will be a new geometry that will come about. I would still count on the self-interest of countries, their sensibilities and their desire ultimately to stabilize their own lives as a driving force. I think that is the direction we are heading. And we can see that in some of our relationships," he added.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar flagged a lack of “understanding or appreciation or empathy” in the US towards India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism. He also highlighted the growing influence of public opinion on diplomacy, particularly in democratic countries. He said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement.

Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate on Tuesday searched the premises of former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen and others as part of a money laundering investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), officials said.The searches were carried out at 15 locations in connection with alleged financial irregularities.The ED’s investigation centres on MassArt’s activities, including its Durga Puja ‘Preview Shows’. Article Title: Tata Trusts propose merging 2 firms with Tata Sons to avoid RBI listing mandate
Article Text:
Internal dispute has also affected Tata Sons' leadership, with Noel Tata opposing the board to give chairman N Chandrasekaran another five-year term.

Why the proposal?

Tata Trusts vs Tata Sons board

NEW DELHI: Tata Trusts, which hold a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons, have proposed merging two operating companies with the Tata Group's holding company in a move aimed at taking Tata Sons out of the Reserve Bank of India 's regulatory framework for non-banking financial companies and core investment companies, potentially allowing it to remain unlisted.The Trusts have asked the Tata Sons board to consider merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Pvt Ltd (TESS) and Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE) with Tata Sons and to seek a prior no-objection certificate from the RBI for the proposed restructuring, reported PTI.The proposal comes amid a standoff between Tata Trusts and the Tata Sons board over whether the holding company should remain private or move towards a stock-market listing."The Tata Trusts today, as majority shareholders with a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons Private Limited (TSPL), outlined a strategic reorganisation plan for the company which, when given effect to, would ensure that the reorganised entity would neither be a non-banking financial company (NBFC) nor a core investment company (CIC)," the Trusts said in a statement on Monday.Under the proposed restructuring, TESS and TCE would be amalgamated with Tata Sons.The move would bring operating businesses and their revenues directly into the holding company, changing the composition of Tata Sons' income and assets.The Trusts said that, based on figures as of March 31, 2026, the reorganised entity would have operating revenue of Rs 1,05,043 crore, accounting for 64.3 per cent of its total income. Income from financial assets would stand at Rs 40,072 crore.Its net assets would total Rs 2,00,158 crore, of which investments in Tata Group companies would account for Rs 1,77,120 crore, or less than 90 per cent of net assets.The proposed structure is intended to ensure that Tata Sons no longer meets the regulatory criteria for either an NBFC or a CIC.The Trusts said the merger would have to comply with the RBI's Non-Banking Financial Companies - Voluntary Amalgamation Directions, 2025, including the requirement for a prior no-objection certificate from the central bank."Given that Tata Sons Pvt Ltd (TSPL) will also cease to be a CIC upon the conclusion of the proposed reorganization, TSPL will be required to surrender its certificate of registration," the Trusts said.The proposal does not take effect immediately. The Tata Sons board will first have to consider it, following which the required regulatory approvals would have to be obtained.Also read: Mehli Mistry to leave Tata Med Centre Trust, his 6th such exit The restructuring is aimed at changing Tata Sons' regulatory classification, which is central to the dispute over its listing status.The RBI classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer NBFC in 2022. Entities placed in this category are subject to additional regulatory requirements, including a requirement to list.Tata Sons subsequently sought an exemption from the framework, but the RBI rejected its request in September, leaving the company facing the listing issue.The Tata Trusts have opposed a public listing and have maintained that Tata Sons should remain an unlisted private company. Their boards resolved in July 2025 that all efforts should be made to retain Tata Sons as an unlisted private company.The proposed merger offers an alternative route: instead of complying with the framework applicable to an NBFC/CIC, Tata Sons would seek to alter its business and asset profile so that it no longer falls within those categories.The Trusts said the restructuring would restore an organisational model that existed for much of Tata Sons' history, when operating businesses were housed directly within the parent company. Tata Consultancy Services, for instance, operated as a division of Tata Sons before being demerged as a separate subsidiary in 2004."The proposed amalgamation and consequential steps are in line with regulatory compliance requirements and the unanimous resolutions passed by the Boards of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust in July 2025," the Trusts said.Also read: Ex-CJI, more legal experts back Tata Sons on Chandra's reappointment The latest proposal comes against the backdrop of a broader disagreement between Tata Trusts and the Tata Sons board over the future structure and governance of the holding company.The Trusts, chaired by Noel Tata since October 2024, have consistently opposed listing Tata Sons. The issue has also become linked to the future leadership of the holding company and the tenure of N Chandrasekaran, who has been Tata Sons chairman since 2017.Chandrasekaran had initially been backed by the Trusts for a third five-year term. However, differences emerged over key issues, including the future ownership and listing status of Tata Sons. Chandrasekaran announced in August that he would not offer himself for another term when his tenure ends in February 2027.The situation changed on September 17, when the Tata Sons board voted to give Chandrasekaran another five-year term. Noel Tata voted against the proposal, while the other four directors backed it. The Trusts subsequently questioned the validity of the resolution, arguing that it did not have the required support of their nominee directors.The board has also backed steps towards compliance with the RBI's listing framework, putting it at odds with the Trusts' preference for keeping Tata Sons private.The proposal will now have to be considered by the Tata Sons board and would require regulatory approval, including an RBI no-objection certificate.The Trusts said they would engage with the RBI on all aspects of the proposed reorganisation."The Tata Trusts believe that the proposed reorganization and action plan for compliance would be in the best interests of the Tata Group as well as its stakeholders," the statement said.The Trusts said retaining Tata Sons as an unlisted private company would preserve the group's "more than 100-year-old distinctive and unique organisational structure", which they said has focused on long-term strategic initiatives and nation building.The outcome of the proposal could therefore determine whether Tata Sons has to pursue a stock-market listing or can restructure itself to exit the regulatory framework that triggered the listing requirement in the first place.
Article Summary: Tata Trusts, which hold a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons, have proposed merging two operating companies with the Tata Group's holding company. The Trusts have asked the Tata Sons board to consider merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Pvt Ltd (TESS) and Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE) with Tata Sons. The move would bring operating businesses and their revenues directly into the holding company, changing the composition of Tata Sons' income and assets.

NEW DELHI: In view of a "series of deeply disturbing" egregious crimes against girls and women in Delhi, Supreme Court Monday said it was a systemic failure on the part of Delhi govt and police that they can't provide a safe and secure environment to the public, which is their basic fundamental right, and sought an explanation from the authorities.Referring to the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park, the gang rape and murder of a girl in Swaroop Nagar, and the sexual assault of a girl inside a moving bus that covered a distance of over 47km from Greater Noida to Delhi, SC said that these have raised serious concerns about the safety and security of public spaces in and around the city, and took suo motu cognisance and registered a case. "The right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental guarantee of life and personal liberty enshrined under Article 21 of Constitution," a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said.Also read: 'No basic public safety, expressing solidarity no solution': SC pulls up system amid rising rape cases in Delhi "Public spaces, including parks, roads, buses, Metro stations, subways, foot bridges, etc, cannot be permitted to become zones of high risk due to grossly inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling, or other preventable administrative deficiencies," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Monday said it was a systemic failure on the part of Delhi govt and police that they can't provide a safe and secure environment to the public. "The right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental guarantee of life and personal liberty enshrined under Article 21 of Constitution," the court said.

Article Title: 288 fugitives brought back since 2019: HM Amit Shah
Article Text:
Modi govt brought back 288 fugitives from 36 countries since 2019: Amit Shah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Stating that 288 fugitives were brought back by the Modi govt from 36 countries between 2019 and 2026, home minister Amit Shah Monday launched a new extradition portal to synergise and expedite efforts to secure the custody of the other "wanted" criminals hiding abroad, to face justice in India.Delivering the inaugural address at a conference on 'PRAHAAR, counter-terrorism policy and strategy', Shah emphasised govt's "zero-tolerance" approach towards all forms and manifestations of terrorism and advocated institutionalising an automated counter-terrorism response and a result-oriented approach for each pillar and at every level of the PRAHAAR framework.PRAHAAR, unveiled in Feb this year as the country's first anti-terror doctrine, is an acronym for its seven pillars Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating conditions for terrorism, Aligning international efforts and Recovery & resilience. It aims at criminalising all terrorist acts and starving terrorists, their financiers and supporters of funding, weapons, safe havens and cyber resources, through collaboration among agencies engaged in intelligence collection and investigation.At the conference attended by secretaries of the ministries of home affairs and external affairs, heads of central police forces, state DGPs, anti-terrorism squad heads of all states/UTs and other cutting-edge police officers the home minister called for consistent efforts to strengthen and improvise PRAHAAR strategy through continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishment of a strong and concrete mechanism for the next 10 years.The home minister asked the anti-terror set-up to focus on the percolation of tenets of PRAHAAR right down to the police station level. He called for coordination among the stakeholders to prevent any delay in action against terrorists and exhorted the states to set up dedicated teams to work in tandem with the central agencies to bring back fugitives.Citing the concerted action taken in the last few months against ISI-backed Shahbaz Bhatti network, Shah said close coordination among agencies at central and state level has resulted in busting of more than 40 modules of the network. "More than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals arrested across 15 states," Shah said, adding govt recently declared the network a terrorist organisation under UAPA.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah Monday launched a new extradition portal. Shah emphasised govt's "zero-tolerance" approach towards all forms and manifestations of terrorism. PRAHAAR, unveiled in Feb this year as the country's first anti- terror doctrine, is an acronym for its seven pillars.

Article Title: 'LPU targeted after owner joined BJP': Ex-Punjab CM Channi alleges political motive behind unrest
Article Text:
A series of videos from LPU captured the chaos that unfolded during student protests with footage showing a highway blockade, clashes with police, lathicharge and vehicles being set on fire.

Channi seeks answers over students, losses

Congress attacks govt's response

Police say dialogue was used to defuse tension

Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi has alleged that the protests and violence at Lovely Professional University (LPU) were politically motivated. He claimed the university came under pressure after its founder, Ashok Mittal, joined the BJP Channi also questioned the police response to the unrest and alleged that outsiders entered the campus and took part in the violence."Outsiders went there and engaged in hooliganism. This hooliganism was sponsored by the Police themselves. LPU Founder Ashok Mittal has joined the BJP, and after that, the Aam Aadmi Party government has tried to destroy this University," Channi said.He repeated his allegation that people from outside the university later entered the campus and created trouble."After that, what happened, people from outside came and engaged in hooliganism there," he said.Channi also questioned reports that the university suffered financial losses of around Rs 100 crore during the unrest, while stressing that he could not confirm the figure himself."A loss of around 100 crore rupees, as reported—I don't know for sure—has occurred, so who is responsible?" he asked.He further alleged that students were subjected to excessive force and questioned why action had not been taken against police personnel accused of assaulting them."And after that, students were beaten up severely; who is responsible for that? Why was no action taken against those police officers and personnel who beat up the students so brutally? And why was the situation not handled in time?" he said.Former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa also criticised the government's handling of the situation. He said the authorities should have responded more quickly after students began protesting."What happened in LPU, the govt has acted very late...they should have acted swiftly. Students came to the street, protested. This should not work like this," Randhawa said.Randhawa also rejected State Railway Minister Ravneet Singh Bittu's allegation that the student protest was intended to disrupt an upcoming AAP event. He said students should not be portrayed in such a manner."Students should not be demeaned. This is Bittu's habit to speak like this, which has no meaning. I suggest he not deliver such a statement, being the grandson of a politician, which could fracture the image of the state," he said.Congress Working Committee (CWC) member Bhawar Jitendra Singh, meanwhile, raised allegations of "vote chori" across Punjab."Complaints are being received all across the state on vote chori. He is just a chief of the ECI. But the system, BJP, which is involved in it must be discussed."Punjab director general of police Gaurav Yadav said police had exercised restraint and relied on dialogue to bring the situation under control after a large number of students gathered at LPU following "late-night rumours about certain incidents".Yadav said the unrest began during the intervening night of September 26 and 27. Students gathered on the campus, followed by some vandalism and the setting on fire of part of a gate.Senior police officers, including DIG Jalandhar Range Navin Singla and Kapurthala SSP, reached the university. Police then held discussions with students to hear their grievances against the university administration.
Article Summary: Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi has alleged that the protests and violence at Lovely Professional University (LPU) were politically motivated. He claimed the university came under pressure after its founder, Ashok Mittal, joined the BJP. Channi also questioned the police response to the unrest and alleged that outsiders entered the campus.

Article Title: 'Full disclosure of electoral roll changes': Congress's 5 demands amid EC SIR row
Article Text:
Congress attacks EC over SIR row, says will fight ‘to save’ voters’ rights (Image source: X)

Kharge backs Rahul Gandhi’s voter-roll allegations

Congress lists five demands

Full data on major changes to voter lists should be made public.

Voters whose names have been removed should receive complete information and a full opportunity to appeal.

Political parties should receive voter lists and essential related data in a simple format and in a timely manner.

Serious discrepancies should be independently investigated within a fixed timeframe.

Election-related data and decisions should be transparent so that no political party can claim information is being withheld.

“The most important thing is that India's voters must have the confidence that their vote is secure,” Kharge said.

Kharge targets PM Modi, Shah and Election Commission

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Tuesday accused the Election Commission of compromising the integrity of the electoral process through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls and changes to voter-enrolment rules. He also stated that the party would step up its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the government.Addressing the Congress Working Committee (CWC) meeting, Kharge said the party faced a “historic responsibility” to protect democracy and the Constitution, drawing a parallel between the Congress’ fight for voting rights during British rule and its current campaign over voter rolls.He alleged that names were being removed from electoral rolls “at the behest of the BJP and the Modi government” and accused the CEC of becoming a “puppet” of the government.On the contrary the Election Commission has maintained that its decisions have full legal sanction and that differing views among commissioners are part of institutional deliberations.Kharge also targeted changes to Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters.He alleged that the rules had been changed in a way that could disenfranchise young voters. He also contrasted Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government with the decision of the Rajiv Gandhi government in 1988 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18.“They didn't provide jobs, and now they don't even want to give the right to vote,” Kharge said, alleging that the government feared questions from the youth.Also read: ‘All SIR rollout decisions unanimous’: EC says agendas for all meetings to be circulated in advance Kharge congratulated Rahul Gandhi for raising questions over voter rolls in Mahadevpuram, Aland and constituencies in Haryana and Maharashtra.He referred to allegations involving duplicate voters, doubtful addresses, multiple voters registered at the same address and entries linked to Form 6, saying the Election Commission should have acted on the issues.“If the Election Commission had shown even a little seriousness in that direction, they would not be in the dock today, and their credibility would have been preserved,” he said.Kharge also praised Congress workers who organised protests at the block, district and state levels following Rahul's campaign.The Congress has been pressing for Kumar's resignation amid a controversy over reported differences within the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. The poll panel has said that operational queries raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi were part of normal institutional deliberations and that its orders followed established procedures.Kharge also questioned the decision-making process behind SIR, asking whether it was wrong to seek clarity on who approved the exercise and why the two election commissioners were allegedly kept out of the internal portal.Kharge laid out five demands that he said the Congress would pursue:He said the Congress did not view the issue merely as a contest over winning or losing elections, arguing that governments may change but democracy and the Constitution were permanent.Kharge also accused the BJP and RSS of systematically weakening independent institutions and said the Congress wanted the Election Commission to be strong enough to command the trust of both the ruling party and opposition.He alleged that two election commissioners had themselves described the CEC's actions as arbitrary and unfair and said those responsible should be removed.Kharge also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation “on moral grounds”, alleging that the CEC had acted under his pressure.The Congress president compared the current controversy with demonetisation, calling the alleged removal of voters from electoral rolls “vote demonetisation”.“In demonetisation, the poor stood in line. In vote demonetisation, the poor has been thrown out of the line altogether,” he said, arguing that voting was the biggest political tool available to poor, Dalit and marginalised citizens.The CWC meeting comes ahead of a meeting of opposition INDIA bloc parties on Wednesday, where a joint strategy on the SIR controversy and the demand for Kumar's removal is expected to be discussed. The opposition is also considering another removal notice against the CEC in Parliament.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accuses the Election Commission of compromising the integrity of the electoral process. He says names are being removed from electoral rolls “at the behest of the BJP and the Modi government’ Kharge also accuses the CEC of becoming a “puppet” of the government.

Article Title: Confession can't be sole ground to convict a person under NSA: SC fines UP govt Rs 10 lakh
Article Text:
Tensions escalated in Sambhal in November 2024 during a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday imposed a cost of Rs 10 lakh on the Uttar Pradesh government, holding that a confession statement by an accused cannot, by itself, form the basis for his detention under the National Security Act (NSA).Uttar Pradesh Police had invoked the NSA against Mulla Afroz in October 2025 over his alleged involvement in the 2024 communal violence in Sambhal.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu delivered the judgment while quashing Afroz’s preventive detention.The NSA empowers the Centre and state governments to detain individuals to prevent them from acting in a manner deemed “prejudicial to the defence of India”. Detention can be ordered for up to 12 months, although it can be revoked earlier.Tensions escalated in Sambhal in November 2024 during a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid, following claims that a Harihar temple had previously stood at the site.On November 24, during the second round of the survey, protesters clashed with security personnel. The violence left four people dead and dozens injured.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Police had invoked the NSA against Mulla Afroz in October 2025 over his alleged involvement in the 2024 communal violence in Sambhal. The NSA empowers the Centre and state governments to detain individuals to prevent them from acting in a manner deemed ‘prejudicial to the defence of India’

Engines and flight data being examined

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has found that Garg Aviation did not fully follow required flight-monitoring procedures before its training aircraft crashed near Kanpur on August 27, killing an instructor and a trainee pilot.The seven-page preliminary report also recommends that the Directorate General of Civil Aviation issue clearer guidelines on how Flying Training Organisations should monitor flight data.The Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft crashed near the Ganga Barrage less than 20 minutes after taking off from Kanpur's civil aerodrome. The 39-year-old instructor and 28-year-old trainee were killed.AAIB said Garg Aviation told investigators that it carried out random checks of data from the aircraft's Garmin system. However, the operator could not provide records of those checks and did not have a Standard Operating Procedure explaining how the monitoring was conducted or what limits would trigger further action."When queried on flight data monitoring, the FTO stated that random monitoring of Garmin data was being carried out; however, no records of such monitoring were maintained, and there was no SOP defining how the monitoring was conducted or what exceedance limits were considered for it," AAIB said.The Garmin data card acts as a type of flight-data recorder for small aircraft. AAIB said interim safety recommendations were necessary and called for stricter compliance with flight-data monitoring requirements."Further, DGCA may issue specific guidelines detailing the procedure to be followed for flight data monitoring, which shall be made part of the TPM," the probe agency said. TPM refers to the Training and Procedure Manual.The aircraft, registered as VT-NBV, took off at around 11.11 am on August 27. About 14 minutes later, it made a radio call saying operations were normal and that it would contact the controller again after 10 minutes.That call never came."No further call was received from VT-NBV thereafter. The RT controller attempted to contact VT-NBV but received no response," AAIB said.The aircraft had no distress call before the crash. Garg Aviation was informed at around 12.10 pm that the plane had force-landed in the Ganga Barrage area, after which the company's team went to the site.AAIB said local residents had reported the crash through the 112 emergency helpline. Police and ambulance teams reached the site and took both occupants to a hospital in Kanpur, where they were declared dead.Investigators have recovered the Garmin data card from the wreckage and downloaded its information for analysis. Both engines have also been recovered and quarantined for detailed examination."Both engines have been retrieved and quarantined for further detailed examination. The investigation team is coordinating with the OEM for further examination," it said. OEM refers to Original Equipment Manufacturer.The investigation also involves Italy's ANSV and the US National Transportation Safety Board, which have each appointed an accredited representative. Tecnam has also provided a technical adviser.AAIB has sought documents relating to the aircraft and its operating crew from the DGCA as the investigation continues.The crash occurred at Kanpur's civil aerodrome, an uncontrolled aerodrome managed and maintained by the Airports Authority of India. An uncontrolled aerodrome does not have an operating control tower.
Article Summary: Aircraft stopped responding after final radio call. Aircraft had no distress call before the crash. Garg Aviation told investigators that it carried out random checks of data from the aircraft's Garmin system. No records of such monitoring were maintained, and there was no SOP defining how the monitoring was conducted.

Article Title: Punjab's election drug debate has old players in new roles: BJP, Congress attack as AAP defends its record
Article Text:
Punjab’s drug debate returns ahead of 2027

"The sarpanch is also responsible for my death. I had questioned Cheema about drugs. My son takes drugs. My house was sold. I don't have anything and finally now I have consumed poison.

The problem of drugs has not been solved anywhere in Punjab."

BJP takes the drug battle on the road

BJP leader Anurag Thakur said the state has to be made 'Aam Aadmi Party Mukt' for turning it into 'Nasha Mukt'

From four weeks to three months: Punjab's many deadlines

Congress, SAD join the attack

Punjab finance minister blamed BJP-SAD for the drug menace in the state,

Channi hits out at AAP govt

Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal has appealed to women in Punjab to unite and launch an 'andolan'

AAP hits back: What about the years before 2022?

Beyond the blame game, what do numbers say

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Punjab has seen this cycle before

NEW DELHI:Those were among the last recorded words of Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old Dalit man from Dirba in Sangrur district, before his death. His family alleged that he had been pushed to the edge after questioning Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the easy availability of drugs in the area.Gulzar died, but his words reverberated across poll-bound Punjab. The BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal trained their guns on the Bhagwant Mann government, accusing it of failing to control the drug menace. AAP hit back, questioning their own records in power.Drugs have shadowed election after election in the state. Captain Amarinder Singh went into the 2017 polls promising to break the backbone of the drug trade within four weeks. Five years later, AAP sought votes with its own promise of eliminating the menace within months.Now, with Punjab headed for another assembly election in 2027, drugs are again moving to the centre of the conversation.Only the roles have changed.AAP, which once attacked Congress and the SAD-BJP government from the outside, now has nearly five years in office to defend. Congress wants to use AAP's old promises against it. And the BJP, still trying to expand its footprint in Punjab, has launched perhaps its biggest statewide campaign yet around the issue.Leading the opposition charge is the BJP, which has the weakest presence in the state as of now, but is making the strongest pitch for power.The Punjab BJP, on September 18, launched its 13-day 'Nasha Mukt Yatra' to turn its anti-drug campaign into a statewide political roadshow ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. The party divided its campaign into four yatras covering nearly 4,000 km and all 117 assembly constituencies.The campaign will end on September 30, with Union home minister Amit Shah likely to address the concluding rally. All the top BJP leaders including Union ministers and party chief ministers from other states have joined the campaign against drugs in Punjab.Yet the BJP has a political history to answer for too. For 10 years, from 2007 to 2017, it shared power with the Shiromani Akali Dal, the period AAP repeatedly points to whenever its record on drugs is questioned.Ahead of the 2017 election, Amarinder Singh's four-week promise became one of the defining messages of the Congress campaign. He later clarified that his pledge was about breaking the backbone of the drug supply chain rather than completely eliminating every trace of drugs within a month.By 2022, the roles had changed. AAP was the challenger and Arvind Kejriwal and other party leaders promised quick action, speaking of tackling the menace within three to four months of forming the government.The BJP has done its homework well. It knows that the drug menace in Punjab is deep-rooted and hence has sought a timeframe of two years to eradicate it. However, Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has claimed that the BJP will destroy and eliminate the entire drug network within six months if voted to power in the state.Therein lies Punjab's problem: Congress cannot remind AAP about its three-month promise without being reminded of its own four-week vow. BJP cannot attack AAP without being taken back to its decade in government with SAD.Almost every party pointing fingers today has a past of its own to explain.The Congress narrative on the drug menace seems to have been lost in the face of BJP’s high-decibel anti-drug campaign. The party, which for a long time was struggling to set its own house in order amid infighting, has done little till now to capitalise on the alleged failures of the AAP government to tackle the drug menace.The first big Congress show on the ground was only after Sachin Pilot took charge as state incharge and managed to get the rival state unit factions on one stage to protest against Punjab minister Cheema over the suicide of Gulzar.Pilot said: “If someone raises their voice against drugs, they face such attacks. I believe the government can go to any extent to suppress and conceal these voices. There are two sets of laws in the country, one for ministers and another for the common man. This cannot go on. I feel the government is completely on the back foot regarding the issue of drugs.”He then turned to AAP's pre-2022 promise: “The Aam Aadmi Party had promised in Punjab that they would eliminate the drug menace within three months of forming the government. They stand completely exposed. I sense a stir for change in Punjab, and change will happen.”Leader of opposition Partap Singh Bajwa has blamed both the AAP-led state government and the BJP-led Union government for turning the state's drug crisis into a political blame game instead of dismantling the drug supply chain.“Bhagwant Mann cannot wash his hands of responsibility by talking about cross-border, the BSF and Mundra Port. At the same time, the BJP cannot absolve itself by blaming Punjab while the international border, ports and the national drug-trafficking network fall within areas where the Union government has a critical responsibility. Punjab's youth need action, not a Mann-Modi blame-game,” Bajwa said.The Congress challenge is daunting. While on the one hand it has to target the AAP government’s failures, on the other, it also has to prevent the BJP from running away with the anti-drug fight initiative.SAD faces much the same problem. Bikram Singh Majithia recently took a jibe at the Punjab government when he said: “Under AAP's regime, delivery of drugs is faster than that of food.”Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal has also appealed to women in Punjab to unite and launch an ‘andolan’ to free the state from the drug menace, including through ‘thikri pehra’, a community policing practice in which people guard their localities during emergencies.AAP's response is to ask its rivals to look backwards before judging the Mann government.Punjab minister Cheema, who is at the centre of the row over Gulzar’s suicide, shifted the blame to the BJP and the SAD.“The BJP should look at its own record. The drug menace intensified during the 10 years of the SAD-BJP government from 2007 to 2017. It was during that period that terms such as 'chitta' and 'smack' became widely associated with Punjab, with countless young lives being destroyed by addiction,” Cheema said.Countering the BJP offensive, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has alleged that the majority of narcotics entering the country originate from Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled states and major maritime entry points controlled by the Centre.Kejriwal alleged: “Today, 80% of the drugs are coming from BJP-ruled states - Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, UP, Delhi. Has the BJP failed to stop the drug trade in its own states, or does it not want to stop it? Their government has been in power in Gujarat for thirty years, and the highest drug trade is there. Drugs enter India through Mundra Port, and stopping that is the responsibility of the central BJP government.”Bhagwant Mann, meanwhile, has launched the ‘Soorma’ campaign to honour drug-rehabilitated people with specially crafted ‘Soorma’ rings and T-shirts. The chief minister said the initiative aimed to transform recovered drug victims into “Ambassadors of Hope”, who will lead the fight against addiction at the grassroots.The Mann government has numbers with which to defend itself.Punjab Police says its ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’ campaign has resulted in tens of thousands of cases and arrests. More recent state figures put the tally since March 2025 at 61,824 FIRs, 81,433 arrests and 3,918 kg of heroin seized.AAP presents the numbers as evidence that the state machinery is finally going hard after the networks. Its opponents turn the argument around: if such large quantities are still being seized and so many people are still being arrested, how deeply rooted does the trade remain?High seizures can show a crackdown is working but they can also show the scale of the problem being confronted.The government says its strategy now goes beyond policing. It has expanded treatment and rehabilitation under ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’, with 547 OOAT centres, 219 de-addiction centres and 91 rehabilitation centres, besides programmes involving schools and local communities.For AAP, this forms the other half of its defence: the battle against drugs cannot be measured only through FIRs and seizures but also through treatment and rehabilitation.In 2017, anger over drugs was directed largely at the SAD-BJP government and Congress promised quick action. By 2022, Congress was on the defensive and AAP used the same issue to argue that Punjab's traditional parties had failed. In 2027, AAP is the incumbent being asked many of the questions it once asked others.The slogans have changed and the roles have reversed, but the question has survived different governments and different deadlines: after so many promises to make Punjab drug-free, why is the state heading into yet another election talking about the same problem?
Article Summary: Drugs have shadowed election after election in the state. The BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal trained their guns on the Bhagwant Mann government, accusing it of failing to control the drug menace. AAP, which once attacked Congress and the SAD-BJP government, now has nearly five years in office to defend.

Article Title: To recover fines, link traffic challans to power bills: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC seeks new way to recover traffic fines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday asked govt to adopt an innovative approach to make traffic law violaters pay fines and suggested challans should be linked with electricity bill to force them to pay the penalty or face power disconnection.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Justice K V Viswanathan also suggested that authorities should take steps for blacklisting vehicles with unpaid challans and also block ownership transfers."It is not just sufficient to keep issuing e-challans. Police may issue thousands and lakhs of such e-challans. Question is recovery of fines as sought to be imposed by way of the e-challans...If people are not paying traffic challans, add it to their electricity dues bill. They'll have to pay electricity bills, otherwise the power line will be disconnected. Work it out. In this country, you have to find a way out," the bench said.The court was informed that challans of Rs 45,000 crore have been issued but Rs 25,000 crore has been recovered so far.It also suggested random checks of vehicles to identify those against which e-challans remained unpaid.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asks govt to adopt innovative approach to make traffic law violaters pay fines. Suggests challans should be linked with electricity bill to force them to pay penalty. Justices J B Pardiwala and Justice K V Viswanathan also suggested that authorities should take steps for blacklisting vehicles with unpaid challans.

Article Title: Will Pakistan decide J&K statehood, asks CM Omar
Article Text:
Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah
