SRINAGAR: CM Omar Abdullah said Monday that making J&K statehood conditional on the end of militancy would effectively give Pakistan a say in its restoration, as the assembly passed a resolution for full statehood and set off a BJP walkout over its reference to a 2000 autonomy demand.Omar moved the resolution that calls on Union govt to restore full statehood. It refers to the 2000 assembly resolution accepting the state autonomy committee report and seeking greater autonomy, and a 2024 resolution seeking special status and constitutional guarantees for J&K.National Conference, Congress, PDP, Peoples Conference, Awami Ithaad Party and CPM supported it.BJP’s Sunil Sharma called the resolution “anti-constitutional” and “anti-secular”, saying its reference to the 2000 autonomy resolution amounted to seeking restoration of J&K’s “pre-1953 position”. BJP said it supports restoration of statehood but opposes the resolution in its current form. Its legislators entered the well, shouted “Vande Mataram” and “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” and moved a motion against speaker Abdul Rahim Rather.Omar criticised BJP’s opinion that statehood could be restored only after militancy ends. “Then the decision regarding restoration of the statehood will not be taken directly in New Delhi but it will be taken in Islamabad,” he said, adding if Pakistan is blamed for militancy, making restoration conditional on guns falling silent effectively gives Islamabad a say in when J&K gets statehood.“We are not begging,” Omar said. “We rightfully demand that we have the right to a statehood.”Omar said the resolution was rooted in a promise of restoring statehood and had nothing to do with Article 370, 35A or autonomy. J&K lost statehood and was bifurcated into two Union territories, including Ladakh, in Aug 2019 when Centre also scrapped its special constitutional status.The CM said he had deliberately kept Article 370, 35A and special status out of the resolution to prevent BJP from using them to disrupt proceedings. He also criticised NC members who had moved amendments seeking references to Article 370 and 35A, saying they had provided BJP “an excuse to oppose it”.Omar said Supreme Court had directed Centre to restore statehood “at the earliest” after assembly elections in 2024 and questioned whether two years could qualify as “as soon as possible”. Omar said there was still no clarity on when Centre considered the “right time” for restoration.Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary rejected BJP’s position that J&K’s sensitive location justified its UT status, saying nearly half of India’s states share borders with neighbouring countries.
Article Summary: Omar moved the resolution that calls on Union govt to restore full statehood. It refers to the 2000 assembly resolution accepting the state autonomy committee report. National Conference, Congress, PDP, Peoples Conference, Awami Ithaad Party and CPM supported it. BJP said it supports restoration of statehood but opposes the resolution in its current form.

Article Title: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 cr of 12.10 cr
Article Text:
AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 crore

How other regional parties fared

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party received Rs 12.10 crore in contributions in 2025-26, a 68% drop from the previous financial year, according to its latest report filed with the Election Commission.Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Both gave Rs 5 crore each. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta.The remaining contributions amounted to around Rs 2.10 crore, according to the report.Gupta was elected to the Rajya Sabha on an AAP ticket in October 2025. Trident's Rs 5-crore cheque was dated January 9, 2026, when Gupta was still with the AAP.He joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion, merging two-third of AAP's Rajya Sabha strength into the ruling saffron party in April this year.The AAP had reported contributions of Rs 38.10 crore in 2024-25, compared with Rs 11.06 crore in 2023-24. Prudent Electoral Trust was the party's biggest donor that year, contributing Rs 16.40 crore.The latest filing covers the first full financial year after the AAP lost power in Delhi in February 2025.The party continues to govern Punjab, where Trident is based.The AAP report has 1,202 numbered entries. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora is listed against 12 payments of Rs 10,000 each, adding up to Rs 1.20 lakh.The latest filings of other regional parties also show a decline in contributions compared with 2024-25.The Telugu Desam Party (TDP), which came to power in Andhra Pradesh, reported Rs 58.25 crore in contributions in 2025-26, down from Rs 83.03 crore the previous year. Prudent Electoral Trust was its biggest donor, giving Rs 45 crore, compared with Rs 40 crore in 2024-25.The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which lost power in Andhra Pradesh to the TDP, reported contributions of Rs 24.31 crore. This was sharply lower than the Rs 140.04 crore it reported in 2024-25. Its biggest donor in the latest filing was Goodwood Sanctuary Private Limited, which contributed Rs 10 crore.The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), which lost power in Odisha in 2024, did not report any contribution above Rs 20,000 in its latest filing. The party had reported Rs 60 crore in 2024-25, all of it received in April and May 2024, before the election results.The BJD had also reported no such contributions in 2022-23 and 2023-24, when electoral bonds were still available.Under the rules, political parties have to disclose the names of donors who contribute more than Rs 20,000 in a financial year.However, these contribution reports do not represent a party's total annual income, which is disclosed separately in its audited accounts.
Article Summary: Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta. Gupta joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion.

Article Title: Dhaka begins search for missing Assam woman
Article Text:
The Gauhati High Court

NEW DELHI:

Tribunal declared Assam woman a foreigner, but Gauhati HC set it aside

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bangladesh's home ministry told TOI on Monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old Assam woman Mumtaz Begum, who was sent to Bangladesh in the intervening night of June 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in Dhaka also said they were awaiting official communication from India on the case.Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, additional secretary (Political and Immigration), Bangladesh home ministry, whose office deals with border enforcement, illegal crossings and cross-border deportations, said officials were trying to locate Mumtaz but had no information as of Sunday. The matter was sent to police and other depts late on Sept 27, days after TOI reached out.Gauhati HC on Sept 3 directed MEA to "endeavour to locate Mumtaz in Bangladesh and bring her back". The HC also directed Assam govt to pay her husband Mujammel Hoque Rs 2 lakh interim compensation, observing "she was expelled without her husband or an adult family member being informed". HC found it denied her a chance to challenge it, a violation of democratic due process.Underscoring that basic human rights extend to anyone on Indian soil, the bench directed Assam Police and home dept to "ensure that declared foreign nationals are informed about tribunal orders and that their adult family members are notified before they are moved outside their district".The court criticised the tribunal for stripping her of the "opportunity to challenge the Foreigners Tribunal's opinion before Gauhati HC".With no information in India, TOI contacted journalists, human-rights activists, officials and govt and security establishment sources across Bangladesh, focusing on Sylhet division and adjoining districts, where she could have ended up.A senior Dhaka-based businessman, who wishes to stay anonymous, joined authorities in the search and is working with govt and security contacts. An appeal with her photo and identification details, including Foreigners Identification Portal ID, was published in prominent Bengali newspapers on Sept 22. Bangla daily Manob Kantha also carried her photo and reported on the family's search.Official efforts in Sylhet, however, have found no lead. Sylhet Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sarwar Murshed Shamim said police had "tried to locate Mumtaz within the metropolitan area but had not found her and were continuing the search."Mumtaz, from Nagaon, was declared a foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal. The HC set aside the opinion and ordered fresh consideration, finding deficiencies in its assessment of evidence including 1965 and 1970 voter-list records of her grandfather, her father's 1977 voter-list record and voter ID, Gaonburah and Gaon Panchayat certificates, a school transfer certificate and land records.She appeared before the tribunal on May 30 with her lawyer, after which police took her into custody. She was taken to Juria and Nagaon Sadar police stations, Matia holding centre in Goalpara, then Eraligool holding centre in Sribhumi (June 4-13).Handed to BSF on June 13, she was sent to Bangladesh on June 14 from Kalaincherra, Cachar, BSF told the HC. Three months on, police, authorities and civil-society members are trying to establish where she is.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's home ministry told TOI on Monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old Assam woman Mumtaz Begum. She was sent to Bangladesh in the intervening night of June 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in Dhaka also said they were awaiting official communication from India.

Article Title: Rape cases peaked at 2,199 in 2015, dropped to 1,901 in '25
Article Text: Changes in the law after the Nirbhaya case , which made registration of FIRs mandatory in offences against women, saw rape cases rise from 1,636 in 2013 to 2,166 in 2014 and peak at 2,199 in 2015. Cases fell to 1,699 in 2020 (due to Covid lockdown), the lowest level since 2013 at that point. The number crossed the 2,000-mark again in 2021 and reached 2,141 in 2023. A decline followed, with cases dropping from 2,141 in 2023 to 2,076 in 2024 and further to 1,901 in 2025.

Article Title: Jails are hiring grounds for pro-Khalistan groups; dead drops of ISI modules also under intel lens
Article Text:
Khalistan groups target north India jails to recruit operatives, agencies flag growing threat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Intelligence agencies have flagged attempts by pro-Khalistan groups, including Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), to infiltrate jails in north India and recruit operatives. The move comes amid revelations made by a recently detained operative who disclosed having been inducted and given Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's contact while serving time in Patiala jail.Agencies are now investigating the digital footprint, dead-drop financial channels, and the broader jail recruitment network, sources said. Agencies have also noted how ISI-backed modules are increasingly relying on dead-drop methods to channel funds, supply weapons, and execute covert tasks and have largely replaced physical handovers with pre-designated drop points along isolated highway stretches and border and rural sectors.Drawn straight from the classic spycraft playbook, this method ensures that foreign masterminds or handlers remain completely insulated from the foot soldiers executing their commands on the ground. Arms, ammunition, and untraceable cash, frequently delivered across the border via drones or covert couriers, are hidden at specific coordinates, with retrieval instructions transmitted to local operatives over end-to-end encrypted messaging platforms like Signal.The tactic of leveraging prison networks draws from a pattern highlighted by high-profile incidents like the 2016 Nabha jailbreak, which exposed the nexus between terror outfits and incarcerated criminal groups. Within these facilities, handlers and radicalised inmates target vulnerable, economically distressed prisoners - frequently first-time offenders or petty criminals lacking legal representation and financial support.In the latest instance, agencies recently busted an SFJ-backed module and arrested operative Preetpal Singh, who, along with his associates, had spray-painted anti-Brics and pro-Khalistan graffiti across Delhi and Punjab, filmed the act and sent the video to Pannun. Singh, it turned out, had a prior history of pro-Khalistan activities, having been arrested in 2023 for a similar crime.While in prison, he was provided with a phone number to contact Pannun and execute future tasks. After his release in 2026, Singh established direct contact with Pannun and received Rs 1.5 lakh through a dead-drop location on the Faridkot-Amritsar highway. Preetpal subsequently recruited another inmate, also on bail, for the Delhi assignment.
Article Summary: Intelligence agencies have flagged attempts by pro-Khalistan groups to infiltrate jails in north India and recruit operatives. Move comes amid revelations made by a recently detained operative who disclosed having been inducted and given Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's contact while serving time in Patiala jail.

Article Title: High-speed corridors to link UP with North East

Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari​

NEW DELHI: A 630-km corridor connecting Siliguri in West Bengal with Guwahati (Assam) and Shillong (Meghalaya) will be built at a cost of Rs 61,500 crore, announced road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari Monday.The road transport ministry has also taken up an expressway connectivity project from Gorakhpur (UP) to Siliguri.Once completed, the two corridors will provide high-speed connectivity between Uttar Pradesh and North East.Speaking at an event, Gadkari added that the 630-km corridor, which will be the "lifeline" of North East, will have the mix of construction of greenfield (new) stretches and upgradation of existing highway connectivity to make the end-to-end travel seamless. He said the first leg of the corridor, Siliguri to Guwahati (400 km), will be built at an investment of Rs 30,000 crore and the project alignment is in approval stage.
Article Summary: A 630-km corridor connecting Siliguri in West Bengal with Guwahati (Assam) and Shillong (Meghalaya) will be built at a cost of Rs 61,500 crore, announced road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari. The road transport ministry has also taken up an expressway connectivity project from Gorakhpur (UP) toSiliguri.

NEW DELHI: Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat's inimitable bravery in the battle of Nuranang against the advancing Chinese troops in 1962 is an indelible part of popular lore. A memorial to honour him was built by the Army at the site of his supreme sacrifice in the border region of Arunachal Pradesh.A biographical movie '72 Hours: Martyr Who Never Died' depicting his remarkable story as a soldier of the 4th battalion of Garhwal Rifles was made too. He will perform 'bhoomi pujan' for the project on Nov 17.While the 'Jaswant Garh War Memorial' in Arunachal Pradesh is a draw for visitors and tourists, a museum at the place of his birth is expected to further cement his legacy in his home state, which sends men to the armed forces in large numbers when compared to its relatively small size.Baluni said he had met the martyred soldier's family members who consented to the initiative and appreciated the project. Rawat had enlisted in 4th Garhwal Rifles on Aug 19, 1960, at the young age of 19. He was just 21 when he laid down his life on Nov 17, 1962.

Article Title: Government mulls steps to save rabi crops from drought
Article Text:
Centre gears up for weak rainfall, orders data-driven plan to safeguard rabi crops

NEW DELHI: Apprehending the possibility of deficient rainfall in the upcoming sowing season, Centre Monday discussed contingency measures to minimise its impact on rabi (winter-sown) crops, with Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan calling for data-driven planning, stronger Centre-state coordination, weekly crop monitoring, balanced fertiliser use and water budgeting.Amid indications that the kharif (summer-sown) crops' output may not match last year's level despite progress in acreage, the minister, while addressing farm scientists and policymakers at a national conference, also emphasised the need to drive the rabi strategy through less water-consuming pulses and oilseeds.The conference was convened to discuss the farm strategy, keeping in view the current drought situation in many states so that low moisture content in the soil and shortage of water for irrigation due to deficient rainfall do not impact farming significantly. The sowing of rabi crops such as wheat and mustard begins in Oct.Centre will send teams to Karnataka and Maharashtra to assess the drought situation. Nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected, and the state has already declared a drought, while Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions due to a monsoon rainfall deficit of 30%.
Article Summary: Centre will send teams to Karnataka and Maharashtra to assess the drought situation. Nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected, and the state has already declared a drought. Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions due to a monsoon rainfall deficit of 30%.

Article Title: H1N1 dominates flu strains in India, accounts for 3 out of 4 cases: WHO
Article Text:
H1N1 dominates flu cases in India, found in 3 of 4 positive samples: WHO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: H1N1 is the dominant flu strain detected in India, accounting for three out of every four influenza-positive samples reported in the latest surveillance data, according to World Health Organization (WHO).The finding is from WHO's surveillance data for weeks 36 and 37 of 2026, covering Sept 1 to 14 and updated on Sept 21. Across the South-East Asia region, 817 of 3,632 samples tested positive for influenza, giving an overall positivity rate of 22%.India stood out for a high share of H1N1 among its positive samples. The A(H1N1)pdm09 accounted for 75% of influenza-positive samples in India, compared with 50% across the region. It was also the dominant strain in Bhutan and Thailand, where it accounted for 97% and74% respectively.Dr Rommel Tickoo, senior director, internal medicine, Max hospital, said H1N1 remains a seasonal strain, with higher complication risks for older adults, pregnant women, young children and people with underlying illnesses. He advised vaccination, respiratory hygiene, early testing where appropriate and timely antiviral treatment for high-risk patients.
Article Summary: H1N1 is the dominant flu strain detected in India. It accounts for three out of every four influenza-positive samples reported. Across the South-East Asia region, 817 of 3,632 samples tested positive for influenza, giving an overall positivity rate of 22%.

Article Title: Coast Guard saves sinking tanker with 23 crew off Odisha coast
Article Text:
Indian Coast Guard

NEW DELHI: In an operation to avert a major disaster at sea, Indian Coast Guard Sunday rescued a foreign-flagged tanker carrying 23 crew members and 9,000 tonnes of palm oil after its main engine failed, ballast tanks began flooding and the vessel was dangerously tilted off Odisha coast, reports Surendra Singh.The Belize-flagged MT Seagull 9 sent out a distress call around 7.30am Sunday, when it was 37 nautical miles east-southeast of Paradip. In a post on X Monday, Indian Coast Guard (ICG) said, "... Following a critical distress call from MT Seagull 9 off Paradip, ICGS Vishwast launched a swift & decisive operation to rescue the unstable chemical tanker carrying 9,000 MT palm oil & 23 crew members." ICG said concurrent cargo transfer and de-flooding operations helped prevent the tanker from capsizing.
Article Summary: The Belize-flagged MT Seagull 9 sent out a distress call around 7.30am Sunday, when it was 37 nautical miles east-southeast of Paradip. Indian Coast Guard said concurrent cargo transfer and de-flooding operations helped prevent the tanker from capsizing.

Article Title: Supreme Court: Will fix timeline for FSSAI to enforce front-of-pack labelling
Article Text:
SC rejects FSSAI’s FoPL timeline, says 365-day voluntary rollout unreasonable

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday refused to accept the timeline proposed by FSSAI for the implementation of front-of-pack labelling (FoPL) for food products, including four months' time for framing regulations and a 365-day voluntary implementation period for food businesses after notification, saying it was unreasonable and decided to fix the timeline for the food regulator.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, however, made it clear to the regulator that it has to implement the court's order, which is in the national interest, in true spirit and not delay implementation. It asked why the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had fixed such a long timeframe to implement it as consultations with stakeholders had taken place in 2022."Why voluntary compliance for a year?... Why do you want to start afresh with the exercise of hearing and calling for objections? You started in 2022, what did you do in the last four years?"SC also termed advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi's plea for immediate implementation of FoPL as unreasonable and said it would pass an order to fix all contentious issues.Additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar, appearing for FSSAI, said the process initiated in 2022 was relating to a star-rating system based on an entirely different criterion. The bench, however, said the issue involved was very important and there should not be any more delay."We appreciate your initiative but there is a lot which is required to be done to give meaningful effect to what we want to achieve," SC said.Reserving the order, SC told FSSAI, "Whatever order we now pass will be binding on you, and we expect you to implement it scrupulously. We are undertaking this entire exercise for the good of the nation and for the good of citizens. We will now pronounce the final order. And we will keep it after some time to report due compliance in each and every direction. Do not disappoint us on the day when the matter comes up for reporting compliance. "
Article Summary: SC rejects FSSAI’s FoPL timeline, says 365-day voluntary rollout unreasonable. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran made it clear to the regulator that it has to implement the court's order in true spirit.

Article Title: On deadlines, we must also look within: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: On a petition seeking direction to West Bengal speaker to expeditiously decide the disqualification petitions against rebel TMC MLAs, SC Monday said before setting a deadline for other constitutional authorities, the judiciary must introspect whether it conformed to statutory deadlines for adjudication of cases.When senior advocate Kapil Sibal pressed for seeking a response from the office of the speaker on the three-month-old disqualification petitions, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it will dispose of the petition asking the Supreme Court to abide by its 2020 judgement in Keisham Meghachandra Singh case, fixing a three-month deadline for a decision by the speaker.Sibal said he had no problem with this order but requested the court to examine the set pattern in which speakers delay a decision on disqualification petitions placing a premium to defections.Justice Bagchi said, "We should hold the mirror to ourselves before giving directions. There are so many statutes that require the judiciary to conclude proceedings within a timeframe. We are gloriously in breach of these."The disqualifications were filed on July 8 by TMC against 10 rebel MLAs who formed a separate block.The three-month time period for the speaker to decide the disqualification petitions ends on Oct 8.The CJI-headed bench said, "We have every reason to believe that the speaker of the legislative assembly is fully cognisant of the principles stated in the Keisham Meghachandra Singh ruling and will make all endeavour to take an appropriate decision within that framework."
Article Summary: SC says judiciary must introspect before setting deadlines for other constitutional authorities. The disqualifications were filed on July 8 by TMC against 10 rebel MLAs who formed a separate block. The three-month time period for the speaker to decide the disqualification petitions ends on Oct 8.

NEW DELHI: SC collegium Monday recommended to Union govt to appoint chief justices of Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana - Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyay and Aparesh Kumar Singh - as judges of SC.The collegium comprising CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Vikram Nath, B V Nagarathna, M M Sundresh and P S Narasimha decided to recommend these three names.On acceptance of the recommendation and issuance of warrants of appointments, SC's working strength will increase to 37 judges against the sanctioned strength of 38. With Justice Agarwal's elevation, strength of women judges in SC would increase to two.As the parent high court of Justices Agarwal and Upadhyay is Allahabad HC, its representation in SC would increase to four. Justice Vikram Nath, who will be the next CJI in Feb, and Justice Manoj Mishra also started their judicial careers from Allahabad HC.Justice Agarwal and Justice Upadhyay were appointed judges of Allahabad HC in Nov 2011 while Justice Singh was appointed judge of Jharkhand HC in Jan 2012. Justice Agarwal became CJ of Gujarat HC in July 2023.Justice Upadhyay was appointed CJ of Bombay HC on July 29, 2023 and then CJ of Delhi HC on Jan 21, 2025. He held the first inquiry on discovery of burnt cash at Justice Yashwant Varma's residence in March last year.Justice Singh was appointed Chief Justice of Tripura high court in April 2023 and then appointed CJ of Telangana in July 2025.
Article Summary: Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyay and Aparesh Kumar Singh recommended to Union govt to appoint chief justices of Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana. On acceptance of the recommendation, SC's working strength will increase to 37 judges against sanctioned strength of 38.

Article Title: Won't reopen Sohrabuddin case but will test validity of acquittal of all accused: SC
Article Text:
2005 Sohrabuddin encounter case: SC to test acquittals by trial court, Bombay HC

NEW DELHI: SC Monday agreed to test the validity of acquittal of police officers and all other accused concurrently by the trial court and Bombay high court in the controversial 2005 Sohrabuddin fake encounter case.Appearing for petitioner Rubabuddin Sheikh, brother of Sohrabuddin, senior advocate D Seshadri Naidu told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that his client lost his brother, sister-in-law and brother's friend Tulsiram Prajapati yet the trial court and the HC overlooked critical evidence to acquit all 22 accused, 21 of them police officers from Gujarat, Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh.The CJI-led bench said it would not reopen the case relating to fake encounter killings of Sohrabuddin, who had multiple criminal cases pending against him, or Prajapati, but would examine the strength of testimonies of witnesses.Appearing for some of the acquitted accused, senior advocate K Parameshwar told the bench that HC, in its appellate capacity, had considered the testimony of each of the witnesses before approving the acquittals.The bench asked the CBI and the petitioner to flag important witnesses and their depositions to the SC on the next date of hearing while seeking responses from the acquitted accused to the appeal filed by Rubabuddin.Justice Bagchi said, "It is worrisome that there has been wholesale turning hostile of witnesses. More worrisome is the fact that those who had recorded their statements before the magistrate under Section 164 of Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), they also turned hostile."The petitioner said the high court had failed to discharge its appellate function especially when it was informed in no uncertain terms that the evidence was tainted because of a "tailored investigation" which was aggravated by the actions of an "unprincipled prosecutor".Sohrabuddin and his wife Kauser Bi, along with Prajapati, were allegedly abducted by a team of Gujarat and Rajasthan police in Oct 2005. While Prajapati was allowed to go, Sohrabuddin was killed in a fake encounter, and his wife was allegedly murdered. Prajapati was killed in another fake encounter a year later.
Article Summary: SC to test validity of acquittals by trial court, Bombay HC in 2005 Sohrabuddin fake encounter case. The trial court and the HC overlooked critical evidence to acquit all 22 accused, 21 of them police officers. The CJI-led bench said it would not reopen the case relating to fake encounter killings.
